Çift taraflı tekel: A market structure in which there is a single buyer corresponding to a single seller.
Çok-birimli ihale: The offering for sale, by auction, of more than one product at once.
Çoklu Bölge Fiyatlandırması Sistemi: (Multiple Zone Pricing System): In this method, while the same delivered price is applied to every buyer in a region, the prices differ among the regions.
Çözümleme: The subjection of a financial institution, as a result of the relevant authorities' establishing that it no longer possesses the capital necessary for it to be able to continue its activities, to a special intervention, with the aim of its liquidation, or of its being restored to the capital structure it needs in order to be able to continue its activities.
Çıktı Açığı: The output gap, defined as the difference of the output realized in an economy from its potential level, is an important monetary policy variable in the evaluation of the price pressures in the economy. Under the inflation targeting regime, central banks shape their policies according to the forward-looking inflation expectations rather than realized inflation. Accordingly, in the areas where the output gap is positive, it is estimated that the economy is operating above capacity because of the demand surplus, and that this can cause demand-side inflationary pressure. In contrast, in the areas where the output gap is negative, it is estimated that there is a supply surplus or idle capacity stemming from the weak demand in the economy, and that this too can cause a fall in inflation.
Çıktı piyasası: Or the product market: the markets where the goods and services directed toward final consumption are bought and sold.
Çıktı-faktör eğrisi: Or the expansion path: a graphical tool showing how the factor bundles used by the producer change as total product increases, all else being constant.
Çıpa: It is used to express the magnitudes taken as reference in the economic decision-making processes. For example, the concept of the exchange rate anchor expresses that, following a central bank's making certain commitments for the exchange rate, and with the other economic units also trusting this commitment, the changes in the exchange rate are taken as the basis in the economic decisions taken, and the decisions such as price, wage increase and investment take shape within the framework of the exchange rate policy. In the absence of trust in such an anchor (policy), the selected magnitudes lose these properties. The monetary magnitudes, interest rates, inflation and growth rates are the magnitudes used as 'anchors'. Particularly in recent years, the difficulties arising in the use of magnitudes such as the exchange rate and the interest rate as anchors have generalized the use of inflation for this purpose.
Ödeme Karşılığı Teslimat İlkesi -ÖKT: The link between a securities transfer system and a funds transfer system ensuring that delivery takes place if and only if payment takes place.
Ödeme Karşılığı Ödeme: The method ensuring that a transfer made in one currency takes place if and only if simultaneously with a transfer made in the other currency, in foreign exchange settlement systems.
Ödeme Kuruluşu: The legal person authorized under Law No. 6493 on Payment and Securities Settlement Systems, Payment Services and Electronic Money Institutions in order to provide and carry out payment services.
Ödeme Sistemi: The structure with common rules, offering the infrastructure necessary for the clearing and settlement transactions made with the aim of realizing the fund transfers arising from the transfer orders among three or more participants.
Ödemeler Dengesi: A statistical report prepared in order to obtain the systematic records of the economic transactions that the resident persons in an economy (general government, central bank, banks, other sectors) have carried out, within a certain period, with the persons resident in other economies (non-residents).
Ödenti: In game theory, the profit or loss a player obtains at the end of the strategy it pursues.
Ödenti matrisi: The table showing the different payoffs that will be obtained as a result of the different strategies that more than one player can pursue.
Ölçek ekonomisi: The concept describing how total product is affected when all the production factors are changed at the same rate.
Ölçeğe göre artan getiri: The total product's increasing at a higher rate when all the production factors are increased at a certain rate.
Ölçeğe göre azalan getiri: The total product's increasing at a lower rate when all the production factors are increased at a certain rate.
Ölçeğe göre sabit getiri: The total product's increasing at the same rate when all the production factors are increased at a certain rate.
Ölçüt Kıymet: It is used in the sense of a measurement and comparison criterion. For example, in portfolio management, the benchmark portfolio is the portfolio taken as the basis for measuring the performance (in the sense of return and risk) success of the portfolios formed outside this structure. Another example: benchmark securities are the instruments that have enough liquidity in the market, whose maintenance of this property by the issuing institution is in question, and that form a reference in the market for similar issues.
Ön Proje: The project containing one or several solutions in which the plan, section, view and profiles are indicated — prepared on the basis of the data obtained, including the environmental impact assessment and feasibility reports, according to the precise requirements program of a certain structure, without the necessary land and ground investigations having been made, the information being taken from the existing maps.
Öncelikli Ürün Listesi: The list prepared by the Ministry of Industry and Technology with the aim of identifying the products to be prioritized, taking into account criteria such as foreign trade data, global competitive conditions, local and global demand trends, domestic production competence and capacity, and contribution to sectoral and inter-sectoral technological development.
Öncü gösterge: The measurable factors that develop before a change is seen in the fundamental macroeconomic magnitudes such as national income and inflation.
Önlem güdüsü: The demand for money stemming from the thought of being prepared for the emergencies that may arise in the future.
Örnek Banknot: The banknote whose possibility of circulation has been removed by the writing 'Örnektir Geçmez' (Sample — Not Valid) or 'Specimen' being printed or stapled on it, with the aim of introducing the banknotes to be put into circulation.
Örtük enflasyon hedeflemesi: The monetary policy regime in which it is not explicit how the central bank will use the monetary policy instruments in order to achieve the inflation it targets.
Örtük gider: The expenses that are not incurred directly during the economic activity and that contain no specific payment.
Örtük işbirliği: Firms' or states' secretly agreeing and acting in coordination in ways that benefit one another.
Özel Bütçe: The budget of the institutions such as the Council of Higher Education, the Turkish Language Association, the universities and TÜBİTAK, established as attached to a ministry or in order to carry out a certain public service.
Özel değer ihalesi: The auction environment in which each participant assigns its own value to the object of the auction, and this value is independent of the other participants.
Özel kapsamlı TÜFE: A price index taking as its product basket the product groups contained in the CPI with high predictive power regarding the future of inflation.
Özel Kapsamlı TÜFE Göstergeleri -ÖKTG: The price indices reached through the exclusion of some sub-items from the CPI. In order to be able to measure the effectiveness of the policies implemented within the framework of monetary policy, the items outside the monetary policy's control must be excluded from the CPI. However, since the shocks to inflation can be of different character by period, the probability of a single 'core inflation' indicator excluding all the elements outside monetary policy control is quite low. For this reason, instead of a single indicator that can be called core, special-scope indicators determined in ways that can assist the separation of the different external shocks are used.
Özel mal: Goods that are excludable in consumption and create rivalry.
Özel tüketim harcamaları: Or in short C: the main expenditure heading covering the purchases of goods and services for consumption by the economic units domestically.
Özel Çekme Hakları: The reserve asset created by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) with the aim of contributing to the member countries' existing official reserves, and allocated to the member countries in proportion to their IMF quotas.
Özgül risk: The risk specific to the company/sector and eliminable with sufficient diversification; in Turkish it is also called 'unsystematic risk'.
Özkaynak: All the resources belonging to an organization with legal personality, such as its own money, buildings, vehicles and office equipment.
Özkaynak kârlılığı: The ratio of net profit to equity (Net profit / Equity); the fundamental profitability ratio measuring the profit per shareholder.
Özsermaye çarpanı: The ratio of total assets to equity (Total Assets / Equity); it is the expression of financial leverage in the DuPont analysis. The term 'share segment' is wrong; the correct term is equity.
Ücret: The payments made to the workers hourly, daily or per piece, in return for a certain work.
Ücret-fiyat sarmalı: The self-repeating process in which the increase in wages raises the production costs, thereby reducing aggregate supply, and as a result the general price level rises and raises the wages again.
Ülke Riski: Refers to the probability of loss to which any bank or institution holding, in its portfolio, the direct and/or indirect risk of the debtors in a foreign country is exposed, as a result of the debtors in that country (central government, corporate or other) failing to fulfill, or avoiding, their external obligations owing to the events and uncertainties affecting the economic, social and political conditions. Besides the deteriorated economic, political and social conditions increasing the probability of default in a country; events such as expropriation, moratorium, repudiation of debt, devaluation, and the lack of transparency in the practices of the country's supervisory authority also fall within the scope of country risk. Country risk fundamentally covers sovereign risk, transfer risk and contagion risk, and also includes the categories of indirect exchange rate risk, macroeconomic risk and indirect country risk.
Üretici dengesi: The situation in which total cost is at its lowest, under the total product and factor price constraints.
Üretici fazlası: The difference between the lowest price the seller would accept for a product and the product's higher price in the market.
Üretici fiyat endeksi: Or in short PPI: the price index taking as its product basket the goods and services produced domestically, based on the prices at which they are first offered for sale by their producers.
Üreticisi): The name given to the manufacturing firms that produce parts, equipment or another product for another firm.
Üretim: The process of the conversion of the various production factors into goods and services.
Üretim Akış Şeması: The diagram requested during the application for the investment incentive certificate, in which the investor shows the stages of production of its goods and services, also stating the number of personnel to be employed at each stage. Product Diversification: the type of investment expressing that an investment incentive certificate has been obtained with the aim of increasing the number of varieties of the product produced. Maturity: the period granted for the performance of a work for which a sanction is generally foreseen in the event of non-performance, or for the payment of a debt.
Üretim faktörü: The general name of the resources such as labor, capital and land used as inputs in production.
Üretim fonksiyonu: The mathematical relationship showing how the quantity of product changes depending on the inputs used in the production process.
